incumbent.name: Matt Lehman
incumbent.summary: Matt Lehman, a Berne Republican and insurance agency president, has represented House District 79 since 2008 and is House Majority Floor Leader, a post he was re-elected to in December 2024 {caucus_lehman} {caucus_lehman_leader}.
record: House Majority Floor Leader; serves on the Insurance, Public Policy, and Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development committees {caucus_lehman} {caucus_lehman_leader}. Past president of the National Council of Insurance Legislators (2020–2021) {caucus_lehman}.
April 10, 2025: Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (passed 65-29) {rc_sea1_433}. April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the 2025 budget (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}.

Dec. 5, 2025: Voted no on HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41; he was one of 12 House Republicans voting no {rc_hb1032_28} {icc_hb1032}. On PBS Fort Wayne he said constituents overwhelmingly told him "this is just not the right time to do this" {pbsfw_lehman}.
Jan. 28, 2026: Voted yes on HB 1002, the 2026 electric utility affordability bill (passed 89-4) {rc_hb1002_149}.

2026 session: Authored HEA 1360, which sets new procedures for high volumes of automated and out-of-state public records requests, and sponsored SEA 258, removing state nuclear-energy requirements that duplicate federal oversight {caucus_hea1360}. Supported HEA 1200 on commercial driver's license English proficiency and documentation, citing a Jay County crash {caucus_cdl}.

race_context: House District 79 covers all of Adams County and portions of Jay and Wells counties in northeast Indiana {caucus_lehman}.
Lehman was reelected without opposition in 2024 {wiki_2026}. Both Lehman and Ian G. Richardson were unopposed for their parties' nominations in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.
No debates, forums or local news coverage of the race were found.

Key differences: Richardson's campaign emphasizes raising the minimum wage, medical and medication costs, legalizing and taxing cannabis, and local energy microgrids {richardson_site} {richardson_power}; Lehman's 2026 legislative work focused on public records, energy regulation and commercial driver licensing {caucus_hea1360} {caucus_cdl}.

candidates.summary: Ian G. Richardson is a Bluffton resident who has worked in food service and as a CVS pharmacy technician {richardson_about}. His campaign focuses on wages, medical costs and local energy projects {richardson_site}.
background: Says he has more than 25 years in service work, 20 of them in food service, and has worked as a pharmacy technician for CVS {richardson_about}.

Lists himself as owner/operator of Ian Richardson Co. and a former Allen County Democratic precinct committeeman (Precinct 298, 2021–2025) in his iVoterGuide profile {ivg_richardson}. Lives in Bluffton {richardson_about}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Says "Indiana hasn't given its workers a raise in sixteen years" and that he will raise the minimum wage; supports child care tax credits {richardson_site}.
Wants to "help to reign in the cost of medical care and medications" {richardson_site}; supports a state-backed supplemental health insurance system {ivg_richardson}.
Proposes community-scale microgrids pairing vertical-axis wind turbines with basalt thermal storage, which his campaign says "lowers home energy costs" {richardson_power}.
Supports "holding polluters accountable for our water quality" {richardson_site}.
Supports expanded education spending and education grants {richardson_site}.
Supports legalizing cannabis and taxing it "like tobacco" {richardson_site} {ivg_richardson}.
In his iVoterGuide answers, supports abolishing the Electoral College and ranked choice voting; listed himself as neutral on photo ID for voting {ivg_richardson}.

on_incumbent: Does not name Lehman on his campaign site; says "I've watched Indiana get more expensive while our legislature offers little more than silence" {richardson_about}.
plans: Cites medication costs and dealing with insurers as reasons for running {richardson_about}.
endorsements_finance: His iVoterGuide profile reports an endorsement from the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC {ivg_richardson}. No campaign finance totals found.
gaps: No news coverage of his candidacy found.
No position found on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) or data centers.
His iVoterGuide profile also lists a 2026 food-service job and memberships in several advocacy groups; current employer not confirmed.

His precinct committeeman role was in Allen County, outside District 79; he says he now lives in Bluffton (Wells County). Whether his address is within the district's portion of Wells County was not verified.

candidates.summary: Matt Lehman has represented District 79 since 2008 and is House Majority Floor Leader {caucus_lehman}. He broke with most House Republicans to vote against the 2025 congressional redistricting bill {icc_hb1032}.
background: Insurance agent and president of Bixler Insurance Inc., a Berne-based independent agency; Certified Insurance Counselor since 1995; associate degree in aviation technology from Vincennes University {caucus_lehman}.
Served on the Adams County Council from 1994 to 2008; named Berne Citizen of the Year in 2013 {caucus_lehman}. Lives in Berne {caucus_lehman}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Said he voted no on the 2025 redistricting bill after constituents told him it was not the right time; said he had supported the existing maps three years earlier {pbsfw_lehman}.
"Reliable, affordable energy is critical to Indiana's economic growth"; says SEA 258 reduces "unnecessary red tape" for energy development {caucus_hea1360}.
Says agencies "should not be burdened by bad-faith or automated requests" and that HEA 1360 "puts reasonable guardrails into place to protect access" {caucus_hea1360}.
Named health care access and cost, along with economic development, as areas to examine in 2025 {caucus_lehman_leader}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements about Richardson were found.
plans: Says committee work is "the starting point in tackling issues that constituents are facing" {caucus_lehman_leader}.
endorsements_finance: No 2026 endorsements or campaign finance totals were found.
gaps: No 2026 campaign statements or local news coverage of his reelection bid found.
The House Republican caucus statement on his 2026 session goals (Jan. 5, 2026) returned a 404 and could not be read.
